requirement.text: Adding a product that is already in the cart increases that line's quantity by one instead of adding a second line.

findings.explanation: addItem in src/cart/cart.js finds existing line by productId and increments quantity instead of pushing a new line.

requirement.text: Discount codes are case-insensitive: "SAVE10", "save10" and "Save10" all apply the same 10% discount.

findings.explanation: findDiscount in src/cart/discounts.js only trims the input and looks it up directly in a Map keyed by the exact string 'SAVE10', so lowercase or mixed-case codes like 'save10' or 'Save10' will not match and the discount will not apply.

requirement.text: When the last item is removed, the cart shows the message "Your cart is empty".

findings.explanation: index.html contains a #cart-empty element with text 'Your cart is empty' whose hidden attribute is toggled by isEmpty(cart) in src/app.js's render function, so it shows when the cart becomes empty after removing the last item.

requirement.text: Shipping costs $5.00 per order. Orders whose subtotal before discounts is $50.00 or more ship free. An empty cart shows $0.00 shipping.

findings.explanation: In src/checkout/shipping.js, the free-shipping threshold uses strict greater-than (subtotal > 50) instead of >=, so an order with a subtotal of exactly $50.00 is incorrectly charged $5.00 shipping instead of being free.

requirement.text: Signed-in customers can open an "Order history" page that lists their past orders with the date and total of each.

findings.explanation: There is no account/sign-in feature or order history page in index.html or src/app.js, and no code persists past orders for later retrieval.

requirement.text: The 'Place order' button is disabled unless the cart has at least one item and the email field contains a valid email address (name@domain.tld).

quote.snippet: The "Place order" button stays disabled until the cart has at least one item and the email field contains a valid email address (name@domain.tld).

findings.explanation: src/checkout/place-order.js only checks that the email field is non-empty rather than validating it matches a proper email format (name@domain.tld), so the 'Place order' button can be enabled with invalid email text like 'abc'.

requirement.text: Clicking the enabled 'Place order' button shows the message 'Thanks! Your order is placed.'

quote.snippet: Once it is enabled, clicking it shows "Thanks! Your order is placed."

findings.explanation: src/app.js's checkout-form submit handler sets the order-confirmation text to exactly 'Thanks! Your order is placed.' when the (enabled) Place order button is clicked.
